# Task 12 Stage 1, resubmission for Gate A round 2 (2026-11-20b)

**Status: Stage 1 output after Gate A round 1 failed; before Gate A round 2.** Generated by `python -m conceptual.report` from `runs/task12/stage1/2026-11-20b` (commit `cd21291484`, ledger sha256 `c11fa749e885`, engines sha256 `b4183d2504eb`). Every number is read from those files. Methods: Raymer, *Aircraft Design: A Conceptual Approach*, 2nd ed. (1992), through `conceptual/`. Round 1 record: `docs/reviews/2026-11-20_task12_gateA_round1.md`.

## Summary

- **Recommended concept: tractor**, re-scored with computed rows (section 2). Éder froze the pusher at round 1 on the earlier scoring; the evidence below reverses it, so the concept goes back to him at round 2. Both designs are kept and reported.
- **Tractor with the PBS_TP100**: take-off weight **2,307 lb** (1,046 kg), empty 1,208 lb, fuel 599 lb, payload 500 lb; W/S 18 lb/ft^2, A 10, span 35.8 ft (10.9 m). The pusher with the same engine: 2,630 lb.
- **The engine sets the weight.** With a rubber engine the same aircraft would be 1,729 lb (143 shp). The PBS_TP100 gives 241 shp against 186 needed (ceiling binds) at a datasheet consumption of 0.901 lb/(hp h), against Raymer's 0.5 and 0.6 for large turboprops (Table 3.4): +578 lb. The engine figures come from search extracts of the maker's pages and must be checked against the datasheet (engines.yaml).
- Requirements: 17 checked rows met, 1 not met: R9 negative gust within the negative limit.
- Empty weight: build-up 0.524 of W0, Table 3.1 x 0.95 0.556 (decomposition in section 4).
- First pass (Table 3.1 with sketch values) 2,110 lb. Method tests: `82 passed in 0.35s`.

## 0. What changed after Gate A round 1

| Finding or ruling | Change |
|---|---|
| F1 main gear missing from the balance | Main gear placed by the 15 deg tipback rule (p. 232) and included in the CG; nose-wheel load and propeller clearance checked |
| F2 gust at take-off weight only | Gust at take-off and zero-fuel weight, sea level and mission altitude; the largest sets the limit load |
| F3 q inconsistent with the V-n | Weight equations use q at the design cruise speed V_C (sea-level maximum level speed) |
| F4 crew-item explanation | Decomposition reported (section 4) |
| F5 ceiling grid artefact | Ceiling by bisection with CD0 at altitude; the last passing altitude is reported |
| F6 hard-coded speed text | The mission records which legs the 1.3 V_stall floor set; the text is generated from it |
| F7 constraint diagram | Landing limit searched to 200 lb/ft^2; best-range and best-loiter W/S and the R16 turn added |
| F8 test coverage | Tests for methods without printed values (identities, limits, Table 10.4 against Mattingly's PT6A-42); equation-to-test table (section 10) |
| F9 constants in the code | Moved to the ledger with sources and bands (appendix A) |
| F10 calibration list, polar, propeller | Section 9; drag polar and propeller operating points added |
| F11 trim and rotation | Trim on every mission leg at its fuel state; nose rotation at 0.8 V_TO with the forward CG (p. 432-433); tail enlarged where rotation needs it |
| Engine (Éder: find a small turboprop) | PBS TP100 (241 shp, 135.8 lb, 0.901 lb/(hp h)) fixed; Turbotech TP-R90, PT6A-42 and rubber compared |
| R9 negative limit (Éder: raise it) | Ledger -1.8 (GA utility); see section 7 |

| main-gear length for propeller clearance (computed, shorter is better) | 0.15 | 30 | 78 | 5.0 | 1.93 |

| **weighted score** | | | | **3.80** | **3.47** |

| Quantity | Tractor | Pusher |
|---|---|---|
| W0 (lb) | 2,307 | 2,630 |
| W/S (lb/ft^2) | 18 | 19 |
| A | 10 | 10 |
| main gear length (in) | 30 | 78 |
| horizontal-tail volume scale for rotation | 1.00 | 1.80 |
| limit load factor | 4.28 | 3.99 |
| nose-wheel load, full fuel | 0.157 | 0.251 |
| nose-wheel load, empty | 0.162 | 0.233 |

The pusher's propeller sits at the tail. Keeping 9 in of clearance at a 15 deg rotation (p. 222, 232) needs a 78 in main gear. The tipback rule then moves the wheels aft and overloads the nose wheel, and the higher CG and longer wheelbase need a larger tail to rotate. A raised thrust line or a tail bumper that limits rotation could relieve it; neither is modelled. Criterion weights and the qualitative grades are judgements, stated for Éder.

Empty-fraction decomposition (reviewer finding F4):

| Quantity | Fraction of W0 |
|---|---|
| component build-up with composite factors (this design) | 0.524 |
| same build-up without the Table 15.4 composite factors | 0.559 |
| crew items Raymer's GA set would add: furnishings (15.59); air conditioning (15.58) is zero with no crew | 0.030 |
| metal build-up plus crew items | 0.589 |
| Table 3.1 fit, general aviation single | 0.586 |
| Table 3.1 fit x 0.95 (composite) | 0.556 |
| Table 6.2 fit x 0.95 | 0.685 |
| Table 15.2 approximate group weights | 0.529 |

Like for like (metal, with crew items) the group equations sit 0.004 of W0 above the Table 3.1 fit at this size; the crew items are 0.030. The build-up and the fit therefore differ for more than the crew deduction; Stage 3's independent sizing (Anderson ch. 8) is the check.

Used outside its calibration (each carried with a band or flagged for Stage 3):

- Table 3.1 and Table 6.2 empty-weight fits and the GA group weights (15.46)-(15.57): crewed aircraft, used without crew items.
- Table 6.3 fuselage length: crewed aircraft; it sets the tail arm and the fuselage wetted area.
- Table 3.4 consumption (rubber, TP-R90 and PT6A-42 rows): large turboprops. The TP100 uses its datasheet cruise value also at loiter; its part-power value is unknown.
- Table 10.4 turboprop weight and size: 400-5,000 bhp; the rubber engine and the TP100 are below it.
- (13.9) power lapse: piston engines, applied to turboprops.
- (12.49) span efficiency: a straight-wing fit; it sets the optimum aspect ratio.
- Downwash: the far-wake value in place of Raymer's chart.
- Gear and tyre drag per area: DR-1's readings of Raymer's gear-drag table.

## 11. Open items for Gate A round 2

1. **Concept**: the computed rows favour the tractor (3.80 against 3.47); the round 1 freeze was the pusher.
2. **Negative gust**: -2.28 at zero-fuel weight against -1.8.
3. **The 1.3 V_stall speed floor** (it sets the loiter speed) and **R16** (30 deg bank at loiter): not yet ruled.
4. **Engine data**: the PBS_TP100 figures are search extracts; the datasheet must be read before Gate B. Its part-power consumption at loiter is unknown (the cruise value is used).
5. The rotation and trim checks rest on two assumed tail lift limits (ledger).
